solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Largely connect thus with leader of students on course

indicators.note: largely means for the most part, so the word loses its final letter
a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: to clasp is to connect or fasten, cut short here
sic is Latin for thus, used to flag a quoted error
the initial letter of students

explanation.surface: A tutor tries to link things together with the head student on a course.
explanation.walkthrough: CLASP loses its last letter, then SIC and S follow. 'On' joins the wordplay to the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Classics is a university course of study covering ancient Greek and Latin language and literature.

clue.text: Learners, extremely unfulfilled in school, worked together

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters survive
being in something means sitting inside it, so these letters go within the outer word

blocks.note: L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate; two of them
the first and last letters of unfulfilled
a co-ed is a coeducational school taking both boys and girls

explanation.surface: Pupils who skimped on their work at school got together to cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner-driver plate letter, and CO-ED is a mixed school taking both boys and girls; 'extremely' wants only the two ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To collude is to cooperate secretly, usually for some dishonest purpose, which is working together.

clue.text: A state’s hoard

blocks.note: taken as written
Mass. is the abbreviation for Massachusetts, a US state

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s reads as a possessive but stands for 'is', linking wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoard is to collect and store up a stock of goods, which is to accumulate or gather.

clue.text: Handbook useful to under-12s talent spotters?

definitions.text: Handbook useful to under-12s talent spotters?

blocks.note: surface reading: the famous 1908 manual by Baden-Powell that launched the Scout movement
setter's reading: football talent scouts looking at young lads, who are out searching for promising youngsters

explanation.walkthrough: The title of Baden-Powell's founding Scout manual is read literally as searching for talented young lads.
explanation.definitionFit: The book is literally a handbook, and its title also describes what youth football talent spotters do.

clue.text: Jointly direct arrangement of divorce

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things into a new order, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple are trying to manage their separation jointly.
explanation.walkthrough: Seven letters of the fodder rearrange; 'Jointly' supplies the CO- prefix in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To co-drive is to share the driving or steering, so jointly direct a vehicle or venture.

clue.text: Female drivers keeping weapon near front of handbag

indicators.note: the front of a word is where it starts, so only the opening letter is used
to keep something is to hold it, so the outer piece holds the rest inside

blocks.note: the AA, Automobile Association, is the British motoring organisation for drivers
gat is old slang for a gun
the opening letter of handbag

explanation.surface: Women motorists carry a gun near the top of their handbags.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association, a breakdown service for motorists, and gat is old American gangster slang for a pistol. The definition is merely a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha is a woman's given name, so any example of a female name fits this broad definition.

clue.text: Handed a new abridged version of road movie lacking challenge?

definitions.note: adjectival phrase for a participial phrase; the question mark flags the looseness

indicators.note: abridging shortens a text, so the title loses its last letter

blocks.note: handed means given
taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new
Easy Rider is the 1969 US road movie with Peter Fonda and Dennis Hopper, here cut short

explanation.surface: Someone receives a cut-down version of a road movie with no difficult parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handed a new abridged version' looks like an anagram instruction, but each word is a separate piece; only the film is altered, losing its final R.
explanation.definitionFit: To be given an easy ride is to be treated leniently, facing no tough questions or hard tests.

clue.text: Story about noble king that’s hard to handle?

definitions.note: a descriptive clause standing for a noun; the question mark flags this

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps round another

blocks.note: a tale is a story
a lord is a nobleman
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A tale about a noble king who proves difficult to manage.
explanation.walkthrough: R comes from rex, Latin for king, as on British coins and royal signatures; it is added after the wrapped story.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall order is an idiom for a demanding task, something very difficult to accomplish or deal with.

clue.text: Rare animal? Yes indeed

blocks.note: first meaning: an endangered nocturnal lemur of Madagascar
second meaning: the naval reply of emphatic assent

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an excited confirmation that the creature is rare; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The aye-aye is an endangered Madagascan lemur, and 'aye, aye' is a sailor's emphatic affirmative reply.

clue.text: Asian banker’s problem about say getting a rise

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other
in a down clue, rising means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: a snag is a problem or hitch
e.g. means for example, as does say

explanation.surface: An Asian bank employee has a grievance about a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: A banker in crosswords is often a river, since it has banks; 'getting a rise' suits a down clue, read from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ganges is a great river of India and Bangladesh, and a river is something that has banks.

clue.text: Take look round region, mostly flat countryside

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
going round something encloses it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
land, a region, missing its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone surveys an area that is largely flat rural land.
explanation.walkthrough: Lo is the old exclamation 'behold'. 'Take' simply tells you to perform the operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a vast grassy plain of northern South America, a stretch of level open country.

clue.text: I valued ground near empty lodge in Normandy resort

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its contents, so only its outer letters remain
something ground has been crushed and broken up, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of lodge

explanation.surface: Someone appreciated the land near a vacant lodge at a French seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: The seven letters of 'I valued' plus the two ends of 'lodge' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Deauville is a fashionable seaside town on the Normandy coast of France, known for its racecourse and casino.

clue.text: At university, dividing students is causing worry

blocks.note: a student in residence at university is said to be up
setting is grouping pupils into ability sets

explanation.surface: Splitting the student body at a university is proving troubling.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' is British usage for being at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge; setting is the British school practice of grouping pupils by ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Something upsetting distresses or troubles people, so it is causing them anxiety and concern.

clue.text: Northern Tokyo, surprisingly first to go for it

indicators.note: the opening letter departs, so the word loses its initial
a surprising result is unexpected, so the letters land in an unexpected order

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
the city name without its first letter

explanation.surface: A note about northern Tokyo, where something surprisingly comes first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is a common euphemism for sex, which is what the slang answer means; it hides at the end looking like a mere pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Nooky is jocular slang for sexual activity, and 'it' is a coy euphemism for the same thing.

clue.text: Concentrate carefully at first, going in several directions

indicators.note: at first points to the start of a word, so only its opening letter is kept
going in means entering, so this letter is placed inside the others

blocks.note: the initial letter of carefully
compass points east, south, south, east, north, east

explanation.surface: An instruction to focus hard while moving every which way at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concentrate' reads as a verb but is the noun definition. Compass points E, S and N give the letters for the directions.
explanation.definitionFit: An essence is an extract, a liquid concentrate obtained by distilling or reducing a substance.

clue.text: Investigates fight with ruler, you might say

indicators.note: what you might say is spoken out, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: a Roman ruler and a boxing match, spoken together in a non-rhotic accent

explanation.surface: Someone looks into a quarrel with the head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar plus bout, said in a British accent that drops the R, sounds like the phrase meaning attends to.
explanation.definitionFit: To see about something is to deal with or look into it, a phrasal verb close to investigate.

clue.text: Heard evil eccentric’s in religious meetings

indicators.note: something heard reaches the ear, so the sound is used rather than the spelling

blocks.note: sin is evil and odd is eccentric

explanation.surface: Someone overheard a wicked oddball at church gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: SIN plus ODD'S read together give the sound of the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of clergy and church officials convened to decide matters of doctrine and administration.

clue.text: Form of sugar supplement briefly included in prescription

indicators.note: said briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter
being included in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: an extra is a supplement, cut short here
a dose is the amount of medicine prescribed

explanation.surface: A sugar-based supplement has been added to a doctor's prescription.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of sugar' looks as if it could be wordplay, but it is the whole definition; the prescription is the amount of medicine prescribed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dextrose is the dextrorotatory form of glucose, a simple sugar found in plants and blood.

clue.text: Increase, after reflection, cost in bar

indicators.note: in means inside, so this piece is placed within the other
a reflection in a mirror shows things the wrong way round

blocks.note: a fee is a cost or charge
a pub is a bar

explanation.surface: Having thought it over, the pub raises its prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After reflection' sounds like careful thought but means the letters are mirrored, so the whole is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef up is an informal phrasal verb meaning strengthen or augment, so to increase something.

clue.text: Hardly sparkling wine kept in Piedmont’s borders

indicators.note: a border is an edge, so only the outermost letters are used
something kept in is held inside, so this piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Piedmont
Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont

explanation.surface: A flat sparkling wine is stored within the Piedmont region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardly sparkling wine' looks like one phrase about flat wine; the split comes after 'sparkling'. Asti does come from Piedmont, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone past it is too old to perform well any more, so hardly lively or brilliant.

clue.text: Plain sort of dog?

blocks.note: first meaning: a broad expanse of flat grassland in North America
second meaning: the first word of the name of a burrowing rodent

explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to ask for a plain-looking breed; in fact 'Plain' is a noun, and the 'dog' is a burrowing rodent, the prairie dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a large open grassland, and the prairie dog is a North American ground squirrel.

clue.text: Prison service welcoming new punishment

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so this word holds another inside

blocks.note: pen is short for penitentiary, a prison
an ace is an unreturnable service in tennis
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: The prison service takes in a fresh form of punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prison service' reads as one institution; split it, and the service is the tennis kind, a serve the opponent cannot touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is self-punishment or a religious act of atonement imposed for wrongdoing.

clue.text: With display, order something decorative

blocks.note: pomp is splendid ceremonial display
the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Ceremonial display and an honour make for an ornamental flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit, OM, is a British honour given by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompom is a small woolly ball used as ornamentation on hats, cushions and costumes.

clue.text: Recalled series of Wagnerian operas being broadcast?

indicators.note: a series is a run of consecutive items, so a run of consecutive letters is taken
to recall is to call back, so the letters come back the other way

blocks.note: a string of letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A memory of the Ring cycle of Wagner operas being shown on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Series of Wagnerian operas' calls up the Ring cycle, but the letters are taken straight from the words and read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme on air is going out live over radio or television at that moment.

clue.text: Boat succeeded with unknown German crew?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees
and means with or plus
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z
acht is German for eight, a rowing crew

explanation.surface: A vessel did well with an anonymous German team aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen, so the German word for the number serves.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand yacht is a wheeled land craft with a sail, raced on beaches, so a kind of boat, loosely.

clue.text: Black singer‘s rock sound?

indicators.note: a sound is something heard, so what is said aloud counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: Scylla was the rock opposite the whirlpool Charybdis in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A query whether a black-clad singer's rock music sounds right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black' looks like a description of the singer, but it is her surname: Cilla Black was a 1960s Liverpool pop singer and TV presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cilla Black was a popular British singer and entertainer, so the first name identifies the singer surnamed Black.

clue.text: Advertisement for Top Cat making comeback?

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way you went, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: pro means in favour of, for
No 1, number one, is the top
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: An advert for the cartoon Top Cat as it returns to the screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Cat is a cartoon, but here 'Top' is NO 1 (with 1 as I) and 'Cat' is TOM; together they are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotion is publicity work to boost sales, of which an advertisement is the standard example.

clue.text: One light finally fading at front of old home

indicators.note: something finally fading vanishes at its end, so the last letter is lost

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a glow is a light, cut short here
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A lamp dims at the entrance to an ancient house.
explanation.walkthrough: GLO(W) loses its end; 'at front of' places it before O.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped Inuit dwelling built from blocks of snow, a kind of house.

clue.text: Speech problem is, after short time, admitted by mother

indicators.note: being admitted means let inside, so these letters go within the other word
after places one item behind another, fixing the order of the joined parts

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written
mum is mother

explanation.surface: A mother acknowledges that, after a while, a child's speech difficulty persists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother' looks like part of the surface story, but the word supplies the outer shell; T for time is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutism is the inability or refusal to talk, a disorder affecting the voice and communication.

clue.text: Weight of cheap paper stored in US bank

indicators.note: goods stored in somewhere are kept inside it

blocks.note: a rag is a cheap, low-grade newspaper
a levee is an embankment along a river, an American term

explanation.surface: The value of cheap paper money stored in an American bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US bank' suggests a financial institution, but it is a river embankment.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverage means influence or power to act, as does weight in the sense of clout or authority.
